key_insight: AI Gamestore leverages the rich, ever-growing space of human-designed games as a scalable, open-ended benchmark to evaluate machine general intelligence, avoiding saturation and narrow optimization of conventional static tests.
problem_solved: Existing AI benchmarks are static and narrow, quickly saturated by optimization; this work provides a diverse, extensible evaluation framework that better captures broad, human-like general intelligence.
method: Aggregate a large, continuously expanding catalog of human-created games as evaluation tasks, covering varied mechanics, goals, and modalities.
Standardize execution and scoring via an automated harness and task interface so agents can be run, measured, and compared reproducibly.
Use open-ended selection, diversity metrics, and human-in-the-loop curation to maintain novelty and prevent overfitting to a fixed test set.
impact: Provides practitioners a harder-to-saturate, more representative benchmark for assessing generalization and cross-domain competence; enables continual, community-driven measurement of progress in machine general intelligence.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing game ingestion → standard API/wrapper → agent evaluation → metrics/leaderboard
Diversity heatmap or radial chart illustrating task variety (genres, modalities, mechanics)
Leaderboard/time-series plot showing agent performance growth and resistance to saturation compared to static benchmarks
Sample grid of representative human games with short captions demonstrating task heterogeneity
paper_title: AI Gamestore: Scalable, Open-Ended Evaluation of Machine General Intelligence with Human Games
paper_authors: Lance Ying, Ryan Truong, Prafull Sharma, Kaiya Ivy Zhao, Nathan Cloos
